title: StayEasy
pitch: You are building an app to book verified homestays in Himachal and Uttarakhand. It's a marketplace: you need good hosts and happy travellers. You have ₹1.8 crore from angel investors. In about two years you must reach 50,000 monthly users, earn as much as you spend each month, and keep trust at 55 or more.

stages.title: Find the real problem
stages.situation: You want to help travellers book homestays in the hills of Himachal and Uttarakhand. You have one month to learn what goes wrong today.

options.label: Survey travellers on a travel Facebook group
options.outcome: Most say they want 'luxury stays' and 'cheaper prices'.
options.lesson: Group members who answer surveys aren't always the people who book. Wishes aren't behaviour.

later.note: Travellers who joined for luxury found simple homestays and didn't book again.

options.label: Stay at 15 homestays and talk to hosts and guests for 3 weeks
options.outcome: The real pain: photos online don't match the room, and hosts lose bookings because they can't take online payments.
options.lesson: Living the user's experience shows the trust gap on both sides of the marketplace.

options.label: Copy the big global stay app
options.outcome: You save time but don't know what Indian hill travellers or hosts need.
options.lesson: A copy can't beat the original without knowing where it fails.

stages.title: Pick your first users
stages.situation: Who do you build for first?

options.label: Delhi and Chandigarh families on weekend trips to the hills
options.outcome: Families go 4 to 6 times a year and share good stays with relatives.
options.lesson: A frequent, nearby trip builds habit and word of mouth.

options.label: Every traveller to every Indian destination
options.outcome: You list a few stays everywhere and none are great.
options.lesson: A marketplace needs enough good choice in one place. Spread too thin and users find nothing.

options.label: Foreign backpackers
options.outcome: A good season, then nothing for months.
options.lesson: Users who visit once are hard to build a business on.

later.note: Tourist season ended and visa rules changed. Your backpacker bookings vanished.

stages.title: Build the first version
stages.situation: You have two months to launch.

options.label: 150 homestays you visited yourself, with real photos and a 'verified' badge
options.outcome: Guests find exactly what they saw. Reviews are glowing.
options.lesson: In a stay marketplace, trust in the listing is the product.

options.label: 5,000 listings across India from hotel databases
options.outcome: Lots of choice, but many listings are wrong or closed.
options.lesson: Size without quality ruins trust.

options.label: Let hosts list themselves with no checks
options.outcome: Listings explode. Some are fake.
options.lesson: Unchecked listings invite fraud, and guests blame you.

later.note: Guests arrived at a homestay that didn't exist. Their story went viral.

options.label: Take 12% from hosts, guests pay no extra fee
options.outcome: Guests see the real price. Hosts are happy to pay for bookings they wouldn't get.
options.lesson: A fair cut from the side that gains most keeps both sides happy.

options.label: No fees for 6 months
options.outcome: Bookings pour in. You earn nothing.
options.lesson: Free with no plan trains everyone to expect free.

later.note: You started charging fees. Many hosts moved to direct WhatsApp bookings.

options.label: Add a ₹600 guest fee on every booking
options.outcome: Guests feel tricked at checkout.
options.lesson: Surprise fees at checkout break trust and kill bookings.

stages.title: Launch
stages.situation: How do you get your first big wave of travellers?

options.label: Hosts share your link with past guests, and you post real stay stories
options.detail: Let hosts and guests bring others.
options.outcome: Past guests book again and tell friends.
options.lesson: Using the trust hosts already have is cheap and strong.

options.label: ₹30 lakh on Google and Instagram ads
options.outcome: Lots of visits, many for places you don't have.
options.lesson: Ads that bring people you can't serve waste money.

later.note: Most users from ads searched for Goa and Kerala, found nothing, and left.

options.label: Referral: ₹500 off for both friends
options.outcome: Friends book trips together.
options.lesson: Referrals bring users like your best users.

stages.title: First booking experience
stages.situation: Many users browse but never book. What do you fix?

options.label: Instant booking with a 'free cancellation till 48 hours' promise
options.outcome: First time bookers feel safe and book.
options.lesson: Remove the biggest fear at the moment of decision.

options.label: 'Only 1 room left!' alerts on every listing
options.outcome: Some book in a hurry. Others notice it's always '1 room left'.
options.lesson: Fake urgency works once and breaks trust forever.

options.label: ₹300 coupon if you book in the next hour
options.outcome: Some book. Many wait for the next coupon.
options.lesson: Discounts can train users to wait for deals.

stages.title: Choose your north star
stages.situation: The team needs one number to chase every week.

options.label: Nights stayed where the guest gives 4 stars or more
options.outcome: Teams work on listing quality and host support.
options.lesson: A good north star measures value for both guest and host.

options.label: App downloads
options.outcome: Marketing wins, stays don't.
options.lesson: Downloads don't show value.

options.label: Total booking value
options.outcome: The team chases big luxury bookings and ignores families.
options.lesson: A total can grow while most users are unhappy.

stages.title: Grow the team
stages.situation: You have 12,000 travellers and 400 hosts. Who do you hire?

options.label: A host success team that visits, trains and photographs every new stay
options.outcome: Listings stay accurate. Hosts get better reviews and earn more.
options.lesson: In a marketplace, investing in supply quality lifts the whole product.

options.label: 10 junior developers for new features
options.outcome: Features ship. Listing quality slips.
options.lesson: Features don't fix a supply problem.

later.note: A bug double booked rooms on a long weekend.

options.label: Stay lean, founders visit every homestay
options.outcome: You save money but the founders are always on the road.
options.lesson: Burnout is a real cost.

later.note: Tired founders missed checks, and a few bad stays slipped in.

stages.title: Raise money
stages.situation: Investors are interested. How much do you raise?

options.label: ₹10 crore, promise every hill station in India in a year
options.outcome: Huge cash, huge expectations.
options.lesson: Expanding a marketplace before one region works copies your losses.

later.note: You opened in the North East, Kerala and Goa with too few verified stays. Costs exploded.

options.label: ₹3 crore from founders of travel companies
options.outcome: Enough runway, and investors who know travel seasons.
options.lesson: Smart money brings advice, not just cash.

options.label: Don't raise. Aim for profit.
options.outcome: You stay careful, but growth slows.
options.lesson: Not raising is valid, with a clear path to profit.

stages.title: Build a growth engine
stages.situation: You want growth that keeps going on its own. What do you build?

options.label: Guests share trip photo stories that link to the homestay
options.detail: Every trip markets the next one.
options.outcome: Stories spread in family groups. Friends book the same stays.
options.lesson: When users' happy moments carry your name, growth runs itself.

options.label: TV ads before the summer holidays
options.outcome: A spike from people wanting places you don't cover.
options.lesson: Expensive reach to the wrong people doesn't last.

later.note: Most TV sign ups wanted beach trips and left.

options.label: Add hotels in cities too
options.outcome: Users grow, but you compete with giants in cities.
options.lesson: New categories bring growth and new costs.

stages.title: Earn more per booking
stages.situation: You need more money per traveller. What do you try?

options.label: Paid 'featured' spots for hosts
options.outcome: Some money. Guests wonder if top results are the best or just paid.
options.lesson: Paid placement must be clearly marked.

options.label: Raise your cut to 20%
options.outcome: Revenue jumps. Hosts raise prices or leave.
options.lesson: Squeezing the supply side slows the whole marketplace.

options.label: Local experiences: treks, cooking classes, taxis, booked with the stay
options.detail: Sell the rest of the trip.
options.outcome: Slow start. Then most families add a trek or a taxi.
options.lesson: Selling the next step of the same journey builds margin.

later.note: Experiences took off. Families add one to most trips, with good margins.

stages.title: A giant enters
stages.situation: A big travel app launches 'Hill Homestays' with 40% off.

options.label: Match their discount
options.outcome: Users stay, but you are burning cash fast.
options.lesson: Price wars favour the player with the most money.

later.note: The discount war ended. Your cash is gone, and bargain hunters moved on.

options.label: Ignore price. Double down on verified stays and host care
options.outcome: Some try the giant. Its unverified listings disappoint.
options.lesson: Compete on your strengths.

later.note: Families came back after bad surprises on the giant's listings.

options.label: Pivot to software for homestay owners
options.outcome: Travellers feel dropped. The team is confused.
options.lesson: Running from competition throws away what you built.

stages.title: A crisis
stages.situation: A family found a hidden camera in a homestay booked on your app. It's national news.

options.label: Remove the host, help police, refund and support the family, add room checks
options.detail: Act fast and fix the system.
options.outcome: It costs money, but travellers see you take safety seriously.
options.lesson: Care for the people hurt first, then fix the system that failed.

options.label: Send legal notices to news sites
options.outcome: This becomes the bigger story.
options.lesson: Fighting the press in a safety crisis is a disaster.

options.label: Say hosts are independent, not your responsibility
options.outcome: Users see it as dodging.
options.lesson: Users hold you responsible for everyone on your platform.

stages.title: Hosts want a better deal
stages.situation: Your hosts say your cut is too high in the off season. Some ask guests to book on WhatsApp instead.

options.label: Lower the cut in off season and give hosts free professional photos
options.outcome: Costs rise, but hosts stop going around you.
options.lesson: In a marketplace, both sides need a fair deal.

options.label: Ban hosts who take direct bookings
options.outcome: Many good hosts leave.
options.lesson: Punishing your supply side pushes them to rivals.

options.label: Lower the cut for hosts with great reviews
options.outcome: Top hosts are happy. Others feel left out.
options.lesson: Rewarding quality can work if it's fair.

stages.title: The road to profit
stages.situation: Investors want a clear path to profit before the next round.

options.label: Drop the 30% of towns with the fewest bookings
options.outcome: Some users leave, but costs fall a lot.
options.lesson: Cutting losing parts focuses the business on what works.

options.label: Launch in Goa and Kerala now
options.outcome: Big new costs before the core is profitable.
options.lesson: Expanding to escape problems usually multiplies them.

options.label: Raise your cut 2%
options.outcome: A bit more revenue. Some hosts complain.
options.lesson: Small price changes add up, but watch trust and growth.

events.title: Landslides block the roads
events.situation: Heavy rain causes landslides. Hundreds of guests can't reach their stays.

options.label: Full refunds and free date changes, tell everyone fast
options.outcome: Guests are grateful.
options.lesson: Treat people well when plans fall apart.

options.label: Stick to the cancellation policy
options.outcome: Guests post angry reviews.
options.lesson: A rule followed without care feels cruel.

events.title: Payments fail on a long weekend
events.situation: Your payment partner goes down on a Friday night.

options.label: Let guests pay at the stay and tell hosts
options.outcome: Bookings continue.
options.lesson: Have a backup for your key tools.

options.label: Wait for it to come back
options.outcome: Bookings are lost.
options.lesson: Users don't care whose fault it is.

events.title: A rival poaches your host success head
events.situation: Your head of host success has an offer at double the pay.

options.label: Counter-offer with equity
options.outcome: They stay.
options.lesson: Key people are worth investing in.

options.label: Let them go and promote from within
options.outcome: A few hosts drift away.
options.lesson: Losing key people has a cost.

events.title: Big long weekend
events.situation: A 4-day long weekend is coming. Everyone wants to go to the hills.

options.label: Add more verified stays early and help hosts prepare
options.outcome: Families find rooms and book again.
options.lesson: Prepare for known peaks.

options.label: Run as normal
options.outcome: Overbookings and angry guests.
options.lesson: Failing at the peak hurts trust the most.
